final_answer:
Short answer: No, Client very likely cannot stop paying, and Lessor is very likely not responsible for the defective Trailers. Client's remedy lies against Manufacturer (now in Chapter 7), not Lessor.

1. Finance lease. Under Virginia's UCC Article 2A (Va. Code 8.2A-101 et seq.), a 'finance lease' is a lease where (i) the lessor does not select, manufacture or supply the goods; (ii) the lessor acquires the goods in connection with the lease; and (iii) one of several conditions is met, including that the lessee receives a copy of the supply contract before signing the lease (alternatives: lessee approves the supply contract before signing, or, for a consumer lease, a notice-based alternative). Here Client alone chose the model and negotiated refrigeration specs with Manufacturer; Lessor was a pure financier that bought the Trailers to lease them to Client; and Client got the full purchase agreement (with the warranty) before signing. Those facts fit the definition (8.2A-103(1)(g)). Client is a business, so this is not a consumer lease. I could not retrieve Virginia's own text of 8.2A-103 because the official site was blocked; I rely on the uniform text and secondary summaries, and Virginia is believed to have adopted the uniform provisions.

2. Hell-or-high-water. For a finance lease that is not a consumer lease, the lessee's promises under the lease become irrevocable and independent upon the lessee's acceptance of the goods (8.2A-407(1)). The Lease's 'absolute and unconditional, irrespective of any defense or setoff, counterclaim or recoupment' language is the classic clause, and 8.2A-407 makes it effective even without it. Thus Client must keep paying the $4,400 per month even though the compressors failed and the warranty source is insolvent. Withholding rent is a lessee default exposing Client to Article 2A lessor remedies (acceleration if the lease allows, repossession, damages, return of the equipment, collection of remaining rent less proceeds, plus costs and fees per the Lease).

3. No Lessor warranty. In a finance lease the lessor does not make implied warranties of merchantability or fitness; the 2A-212/213 implied warranties are not given by a finance lessor, and the Lease disclaims any Lessor warranty and routes claims to Manufacturer. A finance lessor also does not warrant against defects because it did not select or supply the goods. Lessor's only warranty-type duties are the warranty of quiet enjoyment/against interference and against interference by lessor's claimants (8.2A-211), which are not implicated by a compressor defect.

4. What Client does have. Under 8.2A-209 the benefit of the supplier's promises and warranties (here the two-year express warranty) extends to the finance lessee to the extent of its leasehold interest, subject to the terms of the warranty and defenses. So Client is the beneficiary of Manufacturer's warranty and can assert claims directly against Manufacturer. Because Manufacturer is in Chapter 7 and the trustee will not honor warranty claims, Client's practical recourse is to file an unsecured proof of claim in the bankruptcy for repair cost, lost-use and consequential damages (subject to the warranty's limits), likely recovering little. Check also: any third-party component warranties (compressor/refrigeration unit makers such as the unit OEM) that run to the lessee through the supply contract (8.2A-209 covers warranties of third parties provided as part of the supply contract); any extended warranty or service contracts; Client's own insurance or product-liability/warranty insurance; and any manufacturer warranty reserve/surety. Client can also pursue and repair the units itself.

5. Caveats that could change the result. (a) Acceptance: the irrevocability attaches on acceptance. Client apparently accepted delivery and ran the units four months. Revocation of acceptance against a lessor under 8.2A-517 is a theoretical argument, but the finance-lease structure and the 'Lessor is not responsible' language make it weak, and the hell-or-high-water clause is generally enforced; I did not verify whether Virginia case law adds any nuance. (b) Lessor misconduct: the lessee may still sue Lessor for Lessor's own breach, fraud, or misrepresentation (e.g., if Lessor made affirmative promises about the equipment or knew of defects); nothing in the facts suggests that. (c) Whether the lease is truly a 'lease' rather than a disguised security interest (it's a 60-month lease at $2,200 per trailer, total $132,000 versus $85,000 cost; check for nominal purchase option, 8.1A-203). That affects remedies/characterization, not likely the hell-or-high-water enforceability between commercial parties. (d) Unconscionability (8.2A-108) is unlikely for a commercial party that had the supply contract. (e) The Lease's terms (default remedies, notice, any assignment of the lease to a funder) should be reviewed. If Lessor assigned the lease, the assignee would take with the same independence.

Recommendation: Resume payments (or negotiate a cure/standstill or modification with Lessor, which may be willing to help given its own recourse issues), file a proof of claim against Manufacturer's estate before the bar date, pursue third-party component warranties, and review the Lease for default cure rights. Do not rely on withholding rent as a self-help remedy.

authorities.title: Irrevocable promises: finance leases
authorities.proposition: In a non-consumer finance lease, lessee's promises become irrevocable and independent upon acceptance of the goods.

authorities.title: Definitions: finance lease
authorities.proposition: Finance lease: lessor does not select, manufacture or supply the goods, acquires them in connection with the lease, and lessee receives a copy of the supply contract before signing (or other alternative).

authorities.title: Lessee under finance lease as beneficiary of supply contract
authorities.proposition: Supplier's promises and warranties extend to finance lessee to the extent of leasehold interest, subject to warranty terms and defenses.

authorities.title: Implied warranties of merchantability and fitness in leases (not applicable to finance lessors)
authorities.proposition: Implied warranties arise from a merchant lessor of the kind of goods; a finance lessor does not give them.

authorities.title: Uniform Commercial Code Article 2A
authorities.proposition: Uniform text of the hell-or-high-water provision matching the Virginia enactment.

claims.text: The transaction is a finance lease because Client selected the Trailers and negotiated specs, Lessor only financed the purchase, and Client received the full supply contract before signing.

Under 8.2A-407 and the Lease's absolute-and-unconditional clause, Client's payment obligation is irrevocable and independent upon acceptance, so Client cannot stop paying because of defects or Manufacturer's bankruptcy.
Lessor is not liable for the defective Trailers: a finance lessor gives no implied warranties and the Lease disclaims any.
Client's recourse is Manufacturer's warranty, extended to Client under 8.2A-209, practically a claim in Manufacturer's Chapter 7.
